about: The Epistle of the Fifth Sunday after Epiphany in the 1962 Roman Missal, also used when its formulary is resumed after Pentecost.

seg.tr: Brethren: Clothe yourselves, as the chosen of God, holy and beloved, with a heart of mercy, kindness, humility, modesty, patience, bearing with each other and pardoning one another, if anyone holds a grievance against someone; just as the Lord has pardoned you, so do you also. But beyond all these, have love, the bond of perfection; and may Christ’s peace, in which you too have been called in one body, exult within your hearts; and be grateful. May Christ’s word dwell abundantly in you, in all wisdom, as you teach and admonish one another through psalms, hymns, and spiritual canticles, singing in grace, in your hearts, to God. All that you do, whether in word or in work, let everything be done in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, offering thanks to God and the Father through Jesus Christ our Lord.

ex.w072: The participle refers to the faithful Paul addresses, although the subject of the sentence is “Verbum” (w063). Such loose nominative participles work as an exhortation. No separate word expresses their subject, an understood you.
ex.w074: Like “docéntes” (w072), the participle refers to the faithful Paul addresses: they are to admonish one another. No separate word expresses its subject.
ex.w083: Like “docéntes” (w072), the participle refers to the faithful Paul addresses, singing to God in their hearts. No separate word expresses its subject.
ex.w096: Omnia is the object of an understood command to the addressees: “do everything”. No separate verb is printed here in Latin. English supplies it to make the sentence clear.
